div.span:
1 Checks the bearer token itself. Azure's own function
keys are not used, for the same reason as on AWS.
2 Acquires a token with its managed identity. No secret
for Azure is stored in the app or in SCM.
3 Maps the session id to a Foundry thread so multi-turn
attacks keep their context.

div.div: The AWS path writes one file and zips it. Azure's deployment tool expects a project, and creating function_app.py on its own and trying to publish it fails because there is nothing to publish. Make the folder first.

• az version, then az login

A separate install from the Azure CLI, and the piece most often missing
• Python 3.11 or 3.12 locally
• An existing resource group and storage account
• Permission to create a role assignment on the Foundry project

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1378px; height: 1px; padding-top: 694px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Both bridges check the bearer token themselves rather than relying on the cloud provider's own request signing, because the platform can send an Authorization header but cannot compute a SigV4 signature or acquire a managed identity token. The provider's native auth has to terminate inside the bridge.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 741px; margin-left: 17px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: The thread map does not survive a cold start

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 761px; margin-left: 19px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The session-to-thread dictionary lives in the process, so it empties
whenever the function app goes cold. Conversations in flight at
that moment lose their history and the later turns of a chained
attack land without the context they were built on.
Tolerable for a short scan. For a long agent-led run, back the map
with Table Storage or Redis keyed on session_id. That is a small
change and it is the difference between a multi-turn result you can
defend and one you cannot.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 741px; margin-left: 717px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Copilot Studio is the wrong door

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 761px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
MS_COPILOT_STUDIO is the only Azure agent connector in the
wizard, and the shared branding makes it read as coverage for
Foundry. It is a different product on a different runtime, and
pointing it at a Foundry agent fails at authentication.
Confirm which one the customer actually runs during discovery.
Foundry means this bridge, a developer, and a day. Copilot Studio
means the native connector, an interactive login, and someone
with access to both the environment and the Entra ID tenant.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1378px; height: 1px; padding-top: 950px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Credential scope is a reason to prefer a bridge even where a native connector exists. A Bedrock model target asks for long-lived IAM keys in a SaaS console; both bridges use an execution role or a managed identity instead, and the only secret in SCM is a token you control.
